```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, warning = TRUE, message = FALSE,
  dev = c("png", "pdf"), dpi = 150, fig.path = "figures/"
)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)
```

Inputs come from `scripts/03_accessibility.py`. Nothing is recomputed here.

```{r load}
DATA <- "../data"

core <- read_csv(file.path(DATA, "core_matrix_long.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
sasa <- read_csv(file.path(DATA, "residue_sasa.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
motif <- read_csv(file.path(DATA, "motif_exposure.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
prov <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(DATA, "provenance.json"))

sprintf(
  "%d folds, generated %s, n_trim=%d per end, biopython %s",
  n_distinct(core$pdb_id), prov$generated_utc,
  prov$parameters$n_trim_per_end, prov$biopython
)
```

## The three-state encoding

`core_state` is deliberately not binary. Carrying `NA` through to the figures
is the point: a residue absent from an isoform is not an exposed residue, and
a reader must be able to see which is which.

```{r states}
core |>
  count(reason, core_state) |>
  arrange(desc(n))
```

If `not_encoded_3R_lacks_exon10` has zero rows, check that the 3R folds really
are labelled `3R` in `data/folds.csv` — a mislabelled isoform silently turns
absent residues into exposed ones.

## Figure 1 — ordered core vs fuzzy coat

```{r fig1, fig.height=5}
fold_order <- core |>
  distinct(pdb_id, disease, fold_label, isoform) |>
  arrange(disease, fold_label) |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s %s (%s)", disease, fold_label, isoform))

fig1_dat <- core |>
  left_join(fold_order, by = c("pdb_id", "disease", "fold_label", "isoform")) |>
  mutate(
    label = fct_rev(factor(label, levels = fold_order$label)),
    state = case_when(
      core_state == 1 ~ "ordered core",
      core_state == 0 ~ "fuzzy coat",
      TRUE            ~ "not in this isoform"
    )
  )

motif_marks <- motif |>
  filter(motif %in% c("PHF6*_VQIINK", "PHF6_VQIVYK")) |>
  distinct(motif, start, end)

fig1 <- ggplot(fig1_dat, aes(resno, label, fill = state)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_vline(
    data = motif_marks, aes(xintercept = start),
    linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.3, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    data = motif_marks, aes(xintercept = end),
    linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.3, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "ordered core"        = "#2b3a67",
      "fuzzy coat"          = "#d9dce3",
      "not in this isoform" = "#f4a259"
    ),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), breaks = seq(0, 441, 50)) +
  labs(
    x = "tau residue (2N4R numbering)", y = NULL,
    title = "Ordered core vs fuzzy coat across tauopathy folds",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Dashed lines: PHF6* (275-280) and PHF6 (306-311).",
      "Orange marks residues the isoform does not encode -- absent, not exposed."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")

fig1
```

## Figure 2 — motif accessibility fingerprint

`frac_buried` is the fraction of a motif's *defined* residues in the ordered
core. Motifs with no defined residues in a fold are `NA` and stay `NA`.

```{r fig2-matrix}
fp <- motif |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s %s (%s)", disease, fold_label, isoform)) |>
  select(label, motif, frac_buried) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = motif, values_from = frac_buried) |>
  tibble::column_to_rownames("label") |>
  as.matrix()

cat(sprintf("%d x %d matrix, %d NA cells\n", nrow(fp), ncol(fp), sum(is.na(fp))))
```

Clustering with `NA` present needs a decision, not a default. `dist()` returns
`NA` for any pair sharing a missing column, which silently breaks `hclust`.
Here distances use pairwise-complete columns and the number of columns each
distance rests on is reported, so a cluster built on two shared motifs is not
mistaken for one built on nine.

```{r fig2-dist}
pairwise_dist <- function(m) {
  n <- nrow(m)
  d <- matrix(NA_real_, n, n, dimnames = list(rownames(m), rownames(m)))
  support <- matrix(0L, n, n, dimnames = list(rownames(m), rownames(m)))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) for (j in seq_len(n)) {
    ok <- !is.na(m[i, ]) & !is.na(m[j, ])
    support[i, j] <- sum(ok)
    if (support[i, j] > 0) {
      # Scale by the number of shared columns so distances stay comparable
      # between pairs that share different numbers of motifs.
      d[i, j] <- sqrt(sum((m[i, ok] - m[j, ok])^2) / support[i, j])
    }
  }
  list(d = d, support = support)
}

pd <- pairwise_dist(fp)
cat(sprintf(
  "distances rest on %d-%d shared motifs (median %d of %d)\n",
  min(pd$support), max(pd$support),
  median(pd$support[upper.tri(pd$support)]), ncol(fp)
))

if (anyNA(pd$d)) {
  warning("some fold pairs share no motif; clustering omitted")
  ord <- rownames(fp)
} else {
  hc <- hclust(as.dist(pd$d), method = "average")
  ord <- rownames(fp)[hc$order]
}
```

```{r fig2, fig.height=5}
fig2_dat <- motif |>
  mutate(
    label = factor(
      sprintf("%s %s (%s)", disease, fold_label, isoform), levels = ord
    ),
    motif = factor(motif, levels = colnames(fp))
  )

fig2 <- ggplot(fig2_dat, aes(motif, label, fill = frac_buried)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(
    data = ~ dplyr::filter(.x, is.na(frac_buried)),
    aes(label = "n/a"), size = 2.6, colour = "grey30"
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "mako", direction = -1, limits = c(0, 1),
    na.value = "grey94", name = "fraction\nburied"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    title = "Fraction of each motif buried in the fibril core",
    subtitle = "n/a = motif not encoded by this fold's isoform"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

fig2
```

## Quantitative accessibility, for comparison with the binary split

The binary core/coat call and the continuous relative SASA should broadly
agree. Where they disagree is interesting: a residue inside the ordered core
can still be surface-exposed on the outer face of the fibril, and those are
exactly the candidate binding sites.

```{r rel-sasa, fig.height=4}
sasa_fold <- sasa |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s %s (%s)", disease, fold_label, isoform))

ggplot(sasa_fold, aes(resno, rel_sasa)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.25, linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~label, ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    x = "tau residue (2N4R numbering)", y = "relative SASA",
    title = "Per-residue relative SASA within the ordered core",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Central layers only. Dashed line: a conventional 25% exposure cut.",
      "Points above it are core residues still available at the fibril surface."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

```{r exposed-core}
sasa_fold |>
  filter(!is.na(rel_sasa), rel_sasa > 0.25) |>
  count(label, name = "n_exposed_core_residues") |>
  arrange(desc(n_exposed_core_residues))
```

## Warnings raised during computation

Read these before trusting anything above.

```{r warnings}
w <- prov$warnings
if (length(w) == 0) {
  cat("none\n")
} else {
  for (pid in names(w)) {
    for (msg in w[[pid]]) cat(sprintf("%s: %s\n", pid, msg))
  }
}
```

```{r session}
sessionInfo()
```
